restrictions: The two messages have 60 and 62 bytes: each is one chunk, one block, one root compression with flags 11, counter 0 and its true block length; the 62-byte message ends in two zero bytes.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every choice of nine state words the two digests agree on digest words 0, 2, 5 and 7, and a second exact construction enumerates such pairs with the round-1 state word Y4 held inside a class of {{members}} values. Heuristic part: a search over 2^{{T}} such pairs, all with Y4 in the class, for one whose remaining 128 digest bits agree. The search works on batches of seven pairs and examines a batch further only if one of its pairs passes a filter on one internal word (rule A, {{rule_conditions}} bit conditions); rule A is not implied by a collision, and a pair that fails it is examined further only if another pair of its batch passes, and is not counted in the success bound.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5; seven trials per 256-bit word in 36-bit lanes on a 16-register load/store machine; a batch has two stages: every batch runs stage A, {{stage_a_ops}} operations (arithmetic, logical and shift operations, comparisons and branches) plus {{stage_a_loads}} loads, and only a batch in which a trial passes rule A runs stage 2, {{stage_2_ops}} operations plus {{stage_2_loads}} loads; with stage 2 counted for {{stage2_share_words}} of the batches, and with the per-alpha setup and the last partial batch of every class loop, a trial is charged {{charge}} operations; no sorting or lookup and no table that grows with the number of trials (one fixed list of {{list_words}} words holds the class members and is read in order); the algorithm halts with failure when {{stage2_budget}} batches have run stage 2 ({{stage2_share_words}} of the batches of a run) or when 2^{{pass_budget}} trials that passed the second test have been processed.

Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word. The success probability 0.39 holds only under heuristics H1, H2 and H3. The factor 2^{{F}} = {{factor}} in H1 is assumed and is not measured by the organizer-run experiments; with the uniform rate instead, the same search needs 2^127 trials and gives time_log2 {{uniform_time}}. No full 2-round collision is exhibited and none was computed.

Six 32-bit constants, the 32-bit word eta that defines the class and three 32-bit constants of rule A are stored in the program ({{advice_bytes}} bytes of advice); the six constants were found by a participant's solver search and chosen by a participant's count of the solutions of a seven-word system, and rule A was read off counts of the same kind; {{class_choice_restr}}; and recomputing the constants and selecting them, eta and rule A is bounded by 2^{{preprocessing_log2}} units and included in the time. memory_log2_bytes {{memory_log2}} covers the memory of that selection (below 2^34 bytes of main memory and below 10 GB of graphics-card memory, as observed by the participant); the search itself needs less than 2^{{online_log2}} bytes. No priority or novelty claim is made; the number of trials is 2^{{T}} instead of 2^128 because a trial is assumed to succeed {{factor}} times more often than a uniform 128-bit value would.

heuristics.statement: Over the algorithm's one random word, the 2^{{T}} enumerated trials behave, with respect to the event that the 128-bit residual R is zero and the trial satisfies rule A, like independent events of probability at least 2^-{{T1}} each (2^{{F}} = {{factor}} times the rate of a uniform 128-bit value), to the extent that the probability that no trial has this event is at most exp(-1/2) + 0.002.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Section 6.4: lengths 60 and 62, the six constants of Section 3.2, the class of Y4 defined by eta = {{eta}} (Lemma Q), contexts indexed by (X12, X13, X14) with {{ctx_ranges}}, the D0 family with parameter alpha, and all {{members}} members of the class for every context and alpha. Rule A is the set of {{rule_conditions}} bit conditions of Section 6.3 on the word h1 of a trial (Lemma A).
heuristics.extrapolation: From a participant count of the class rate under the seven-word model, that is of the number of solutions with Y4 in the class of the seven-word system that determines R. The count is an enumeration without sampling: for each value beta of an auxiliary difference of one of the two calls, every outcome of that call is enumerated, the other call is counted exactly for it, and the probability of the outcome is counted exactly. Over {{betas_list_claim}} ({{betas_with_mass}} of them with a nonzero part){{outside_claim}}, the count is {{exact_total}} times the uniform expectation; values of beta not enumerated are left out, so this is a lower bound under the model. {{recount_short}} Rule A is not implied by R = 0: {{rule_solvers_claim}} no solution violating it for {{rule_ok}} of the {{rule_outcomes}} outcomes of the count; the other {{rule_bad}} are left out in full, leaving {{rule_count}}. A sampler with the same count of the second call, used as a check, gives {{sampler_sum}} with standard error {{sampler_sum_se}} for the {{sampled_betas}} values of beta it was run on, against {{sampled_exact_sum}} counted for them{{sampler_far_claim}}. From checks of the counting program: against the sampler on other constants; of its count for the first call against brute force with 8-bit words{{e1amc_claim}}; {{e3check_claim}}{{review_claim}}. From a comparison of the seven-word model with real trials of the class search for these constants at 32 bits, on events of probability about 2^-32 and above: {{real_notes_claim}}. And from scaled-down end-to-end runs of the same class search with 8-bit and 10-bit words and other constants, comparing the collisions found with the model's exact prediction (9,835 against 9,837.9 predicted at 8 bits, 693 against 664.6 at 10 bits; the same check for the search without the class restriction gave 1,813 against 1,807.2 over ten constant sets and 1,465 runs). {{toyalg_claim}} All in proof.md Section 10. The extrapolation is from these to the rate of the event over 2^{{T}} real trials.
heuristics.limitations: The factor {{factor}} is assumed. It is set against a participant count of {{rule_count}}, {{exact_over_factor}} times larger, which the organizer-run experiments do not measure; the success bound needs a factor of at least {{f_min}}. With factor 1 (the uniform rate) the claim would be 2^127 trials and time_log2 {{uniform_time}}. The count is exact only under the seven-word model, that six of the seven words behave like independent uniform words over the trials; that the trials of the algorithm meet the counted solutions at the model's rate is the assumption. The model is tested on real messages only for events of probability about 2^-32 and above{{deep_limit_claim}}, and end to end only at small word sizes and with other constants (a scaled-down hash with words of {{toy_bits_all}}); its use at the probability of a collision, about 2^-{{hit_exp}}, cannot be tested directly.{{deep_caveats_claim}} Rule A is not implied by a collision; that it loses no more than the figure allows rests {{rule_unsat_claim}}, and rule A was chosen from counts of the same kind. No measurement tests rule A together with R = 0. The constants and the class were chosen to make the count large, by a solver search and by the count itself; {{class_choice_claim}}; the count is deterministic, so no sampling noise enters, but a choice that is best under the model says nothing about the model, and if the model overstates the rate for some constants such a search will tend to find them. The count rests on few paths: {{heaviest_share}}% of it comes from one value of beta and {{top2_share}}% from two. The counting program is not in the package; it and every check of it are the participant's, those of the reviewing helper agents included; its count for the first call and its enumeration of outcomes are new code, checked against brute force only for 8-bit words{{e1amc_limit}}. All trials of a run share the four seed words, trials of one context share most other words, and the {{members}} trials of one context and alpha differ only in Y4 and what follows from it; their independence is assumed, and with a count that rests on few paths it was not examined whether collisions depend on a few shared words. The 32-bit comparison gave every context its own random words. {{layout_claim_limit}} {{run_distribution_claim}} Comparisons of the model with real messages for the constants of an earlier submission showed deviations of up to 3.1 standard deviations in some settings, among them an unexplained spread between two runs. One of the eleven earlier scaled-down class series has a variance-to-mean ratio of its collisions per run of 1.60, about 2.65 standard errors above 1. Nothing here is organizer-verified except the two declared experiments, which do not measure the 128-bit rate and are not a test of H1.

heuristics.statement: With probability at least 0.9995 over the random word, fewer than 2^{{pass_budget}} of the 2^{{T}} trials pass the 32-bit E1 test of proof.md Lemma N without having R = 0.
heuristics.scope: The E1 test of Section 6.3 on all trials of Section 6.4, whether or not their batch runs stage 2; the algorithm processes only the passes in batches that run stage 2, which are fewer. The measured pass rate 2^{{pass_rate}} would give 2^{{pass_expected}} passes; the budget of 2^{{pass_budget}} corresponds to a pass rate of 2^-{{pass_shift}} and is larger by a factor of about 2^{{pass_margin}}, and processing 2^{{pass_budget}} passes is charged in the time bound (2^{{pass_ops}} operations).
heuristics.extrapolation: From participant measurements of the pass rate on {{pass_measured_on}} at 32 bits ({{pass_count}} passes in 2^{{pass_trials}} trials with an independent random context per thread; {{layout_e1_note}}; all in proof.md Section 10, where a pass of the E1 test is called a trial in which E1 requires the class) to the 2^{{T}} trials of one run.
heuristics.limitations: Not organizer-verified. The measured rate is a mean; that the pass count of a full run of 2^{{T}} trials, whose contexts share the four seed words, stays near that mean is assumed{{h2_limit_claim}}. The budget exceeds the passes expected at the measured rate by a factor of about 2^{{pass_margin}}. If the budget were exceeded the algorithm halts with failure, which lowers the success probability but does not raise the time bound; H2 enters the success bound only through its own failure probability of 0.0005.

heuristics.statement: With probability at least 0.9995 over the random word, fewer than {{stage2_budget}} of the 2^{{T}} trials satisfy rule A of proof.md Section 6.3, so that fewer than that many batches run stage 2.
heuristics.scope: Rule A (Lemma A) on the trials of Section 6.4, in the seven-lane batches of Section 6.5. A batch runs stage 2 only if one of its seven trials satisfies rule A, and every trial lies in one batch, so the number of batches that run stage 2 is at most the number of trials that satisfy rule A. The budget is {{stage2_share_words}} of the {{batches_total}} batches of a run, a share 2^{{stage2_trial_share}} of the trials; the time bound charges stage 2 for that many batches, and the algorithm halts with failure when the budget is reached.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the fact that a uniform 32-bit word satisfies the {{rule_conditions}} conditions of rule A with probability 2^-{{rule_pass_exp}}, and from participant measurements on real trials at 32 bits, in runs with shared seed words that are laid out like a run of the algorithm except that X13 is not restricted and one context word is not held fixed: {{a_runs}} runs of 2^{{a_run_trials}} trials each gave {{a_counts}} trials that satisfy rule A, where a share of 2^-{{rule_pass_exp}} is {{a_expected}} ({{a_devs}} binomial standard deviations), a share of 2^{{a_rate}} in all. Seven times that share is at most {{a_share}} of the batches, and the budget of {{stage2_share}} is larger by a factor of {{a_margin}}.{{h3_layout_claim}} The self-test of the submitted program finds the same share of lanes on inputs of its own ({{st_pass_a}} of {{st_lanes}} lanes{{big_claim}}). All in proof.md Sections 6.5 and 10. The extrapolation is from these runs to the 2^{{T}} trials of one run.
heuristics.limitations: Not organizer-verified. The measured share is a mean over {{a_runs}} runs; that no run of 2^{{T}} trials, whose contexts share four seed words, has a share {{a_margin}} times as large is assumed{{h3_exclude_claim}}{{h3_spread_claim}}{{h3_spread_layout}} If the budget were exceeded the algorithm halts with failure, which lowers the success probability but does not raise the time bound; H3 enters the success bound only through its own failure probability of 0.0005. The operation counts of the two stages are the submitted program's own.
